description: Tests for the data-access analyzer on Go code — fmt.Sprintf SQL injection vs $1 parameterized queries. Tenancy is declared in .codeauditor.json (analyzerConfigs.data-access.orgFilterTables: ["users"]), so missing-org-filter has a declared tenant table to check. parameterized.go fires missing-org-filter twice (both critical): its SELECT on users has no org predicate, and its INSERT `(name, email)` omits the tenant column from the column list — Spec 68 §9 makes the INSERT check a column-list predicate (fire only when the row-adding statement does not set the tenant column), format-agnostic for Go and TypeScript alike. The INSERT is still not an unfiltered-query — Spec 68 disposition (a) makes that write set UPDATE-only (a bare DELETE is whole-table maintenance, INSERT is row-adding). Without the declaration the rule's input is absent and the finding would silently read clean instead of firing.
